title: Kindly Regard
note: This is being unable to refuse what people familiar to you say, once you see them. It happens when your eye goes out to them, hence its name. It expands on what the chapter on not ruling by fear said, so it follows that chapter.

couplets.plain: This world exists because of the surpassing beauty called kindly regard.
couplets.pm: Because the surpassing beauty called kindly regard is found in rulers, this world exists. A ruler without it does terrifying things, and the people of his land have no more safety than a herd of deer that has met a tiger.

links.quote: This world exists because of the surpassing beauty
links.reason: Says the world stands only because this kindly regard is in it.

couplets.plain: The way of the world rests on kindly regard. Those without it exist only as a burden on the earth.
couplets.pm: The ways of the world, such as helping others, protecting them and forgiving their mistakes, go on through kindly regard. So those without it exist only to load this earth, for nothing else, since they are of no use to themselves or to anyone.

links.quote: The way of the world rests on kindly regard
links.reason: Rests the whole way of the world on this one grace.

couplets.plain: What use is a melody that doesn’t fit the song? What use is an eye without kindly regard?
couplets.pm: What use is a melody that doesn’t fit the work of singing? In the same way, what use is an eye where there is no kindly regard? A melody is useless unless joined to the techniques of voice and harp, and an eye is useless unless joined to kindly regard.

links.quote: What use is an eye without kindly regard?
links.reason: Sets an eye without kindly regard beside a melody that doesn’t fit the song: both have lost their point.

couplets.plain: Eyes without kindly regard, in due measure, only seem to be there in the face. What else do they do?
couplets.pm: Eyes without a kindly regard that keeps within measure do nothing except seem, to those who look at them, to be in the face. They serve no other purpose. “In measure” rules out too much kindly regard.

links.quote: Eyes without kindly regard, in due measure
only seem to be there in the face

couplets.plain: Kindly regard is the eye’s jewel. Without it, an eye is taken for a sore.
couplets.pm: Kindly regard is the jewel an eye wears, and it has no other. Without it, the wise know that eye for a sore. It may look like an eye, but it brings suffering through its diseases and its clinging to what the senses seize.

links.quote: Kindly regard is the eye’s jewel

links.reason: Names kindly regard as the jewel an eye wears.

links.quote: an eye is taken for a sore

couplets.plain: People who have eyes, yet whose eyes never turn kindly to others, are like trees fixed in the soil.
couplets.pm: Those who have eyes made for turning towards others, and don’t turn them, are like trees standing in the soil, though they walk about. A tree has its “eyes” too, and they don’t turn. He rejects the reading of a wooden doll coated in plaster, because that rests on a hidden core, not on the eye that is seen.

links.quote: whose eyes never turn kindly to others
like trees fixed in the soil

couplets.plain: Those without kindly regard have no eyes. Those who have eyes are never without it.
couplets.pm: Those without kindly regard don’t even have eyes, and those who have eyes are never without it. In people who have eyes, kindly regard moves in the very act of seeing.

links.quote: Those who have eyes are never without it
links.reason: Makes kindly regard the proof of real sight.

links.quote: Those without kindly regard have no eyes
links.reason: Turns blindness into the state of anyone without kindly regard.

couplets.plain: This world belongs to those who can show kindly regard without ruining the work they must do.
couplets.pm: This world is the rightful possession of rulers who can show kindly regard without ruining their work of justice. Justice is ruined when a ruler spares friends who have harmed others. To withhold it where justice would suffer and show it elsewhere is rare, and the whole world comes to such rulers for a long time.

links.quote: show kindly regard without ruining the work

couplets.plain: Even with people whose way is to hurt you, the highest quality is to show kindly regard and put up with it.
couplets.pm: Even towards those whose nature is to hurt them, showing kindly regard and bearing the fault is the foremost quality of a ruler. These are people the ruler knows well, as “whose nature” implies.
couplets.sensitive: counsels forbearance towards those who wrong you

links.quote: Even with people whose way is to hurt you
links.reason: Extends kindly regard even to people whose way is to hurt you.

links.quote: show kindly regard and put up with it
links.reason: Calls bearing with those who hurt you the highest quality.

couplets.plain: Those who want the courtesy everyone admires will watch poison being poured, drink it and stay content.
couplets.pm: Those who want the kindly regard that all desire, even seeing friends put poison in for them, can’t bring themselves to refuse. They drink it and stay close to those friends after. He takes நாகரிகம் as kindly regard. A ruler should spare people in this way only when the wrong is against himself.
couplets.sensitive: praises knowingly accepting harm from another

links.quote: watch poison being poured, drink it
links.reason: Takes the courtesy everyone admires as far as drinking poison rather than refuse the one who poured it.
